title: 32 Mild American Freezer Recipes — No Onions, No Peppers

exclusions: all onions including powders, shallots and scallions
all peppers including bell, chili, paprika, cayenne and black pepper
premade mixed seasoning containing those ingredients
design.flavor_profile: mild familiar comfort foods; garlic generally included unless specified
design.source_policy: Each entry links to a real online recipe example examined for method/freezing suitability; the supplied no-onion/no-pepper versions are original adaptations, not claimed to be tested by original publishers.
design.ingredient_label_warning: Read labels for breads, sauces, mustard, broths, cooked ham, seasonings, cheeses and spice blends. Use plain ingredients or substitute homemade versions where onion or pepper ingredients appear. Recipes cannot guarantee manufacturer formulations.

science_backbone.quality_vs_safety: Quality month estimates assume continuous 0°F or colder and protective packaging. They are quality targets, not safety expiration dates; properly handled food remains safe indefinitely while continuously frozen at 0°F.
science_backbone.safe_chill: Within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour if ambient >90°F), divide into shallow containers and refrigerate or freeze promptly; refrigerate until chilled before tightly sealing and freezing dense meals.
science_backbone.freezing_speed: Use small thin packages and avoid overloading freezer with unfrozen food.
science_backbone.thawing: Refrigerator preferred; sealed food can be thawed under cold water with water changed every 30 min and must be cooked immediately; microwave-thawed food must be cooked promptly; never thaw on counter.
science_backbone.reheat: Reheat cooked leftover meat/casseroles to 165°F measured in center. Soups/sauces bring to rolling boil. For raw freezer kits, follow initial cook temperature and time, not leftover reheating instructions.
science_backbone.packaging: Moisture-vapor-resistant, food-grade freezer bags and tight rigid freezer tubs; expel air from bags. Liquids need expansion headspace. Individually wrap dry items to prevent dehydration.
science_backbone.slow_cooker: Thaw raw meat and poultry in refrigerator before placing in conventional slow cooker.
science_backbone.rice_note: Promptly chill cooked rice in shallow containers, refrigerate promptly and freeze; do not let cooked rice stand at room temperature.
science_backbone.allergen_note: Recipes contain common allergens (wheat, milk, egg, soy); check ingredients and substitute as needed.

recipes.name: Classic Glazed Beef Meatloaf
recipes.equipment: rimmed sheet pan and food thermometer
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Whisk egg and milk. Stir in breadcrumbs, salt, garlic powder and parsley; rest 2 minutes. Gently combine with beef. Mix tomato paste, sugar, vinegar and water for glaze.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Whisk egg and milk. Stir in breadcrumbs, salt, garlic powder and parsley; rest 2 minutes. Gently combine with beef. Mix tomato paste, sugar, vinegar and water for glaze.
numbered_cooking_steps: Preheat oven to 350°F; line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Shape beef mixture into an approximately 9x5-inch loaf, without packing tightly.
Brush with half the glaze; bake 35 minutes. Brush with remaining glaze.
Bake another 20–30 minutes until center reaches 160°F; rest 10 minutes, then slice.
recipes.before_freezing: Chill slices rapidly in shallow containers; freeze with 1 tbsp glaze per slice.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Wrap each 1–2-slice serving tightly in freezer wrap; place in labeled freezer zip bag, push out air.
recipes.thawing: Refrigerate overnight (8–24 hr).
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered at 325°F for about 15–25 min from refrigerator-thawed, to 165°F; add 1 tbsp water and glaze.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Dry edges and crumbly meat after freezing.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Moderate fat and glaze protect proteins against dry reheating; freeze in narrow slices.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Add fresh potatoes/vegetables.

recipe_example_source.adaptation_note: Adapted into an original no-onion, no-pepper formulation; source recipe may contain excluded ingredients and is not identical.

recipes.name: Beef Meatballs in Brown Gravy
ingredients: 2 tsp beef base verified free of onion and pepper ingredients
recipes.oven_bake_time: 16–22 min for meatballs plus 6–8 min for gravy
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Combine beef, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, salt and garlic powder gently; roll into 20 meatballs. Whisk beef base into water.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Combine beef, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, salt and garlic powder gently; roll into 20 meatballs. Whisk beef base into water.
numbered_cooking_steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Arrange meatballs on a parchment-lined sheet pan.
Bake 16–22 min until 160°F internally.
Melt butter in saucepan; whisk in flour 1 min, then slowly whisk in prepared beef liquid; simmer 4–6 min until smooth and thick.
Combine meatballs and gravy; simmer 2 min.
recipes.before_freezing: Rapidly chill meatballs with gravy in shallow 3–5 serving portions.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Airtight freezer-safe rigid boxes, gravy covering meatballs; leave about 1/2 inch expansion space.
recipes.thawing: Fridge overnight.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered saucepan on medium-low 10–15 min after thawing, stir gently to 165°F; thin with 1–2 tbsp water if necessary.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Gravy can thicken or weep; uncovered meatballs dry out.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Gravy encases meatballs and prevents moisture loss.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Fresh mashed potatoes or egg noodles.

recipe_example_source.adaptation_note: Adapted into an original no-onion, no-pepper formulation; source recipe may contain excluded ingredients and is not identical.

recipes.name: Mild Salisbury Steak With Smooth Gravy
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Mix beef, crumbs, egg, tomato paste, salt and garlic powder; make four 3/4-inch thick oval patties. Whisk broth base into water.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Mix beef, crumbs, egg, tomato paste, salt and garlic powder; make four 3/4-inch thick oval patties. Whisk broth base into water.
numbered_cooking_steps: Brown patties in oil over medium-high heat, 3–4 min per side; remove.
Melt butter in skillet and whisk in flour 1 min. Whisk in prepared broth and simmer 2 min.
Return patties to gravy, cover and simmer 8–12 min to 160°F internal temperature.
recipes.before_freezing: Chill patties immersed in thickened gravy.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Flat single-layer freezer boxes with tight lids, minimal air and a little expansion space.
recipes.thawing: Fridge overnight.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered skillet on low-medium 10–15 min to 165°F, add splash of water as needed.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Thin patties dry at edges when uncovered.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Freeze fully submerged in gravy; add starches freshly.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Serve over fresh noodles or potatoes.

recipe_example_source.adaptation_note: Adapted into an original no-onion, no-pepper formulation; source recipe may contain excluded ingredients and is not identical.

recipes.name: Tender Brown-Sugar Pulled Pork
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Mix water, sugar, vinegar, salt, garlic and thyme. Place pork in 5–6 qt slow cooker; pour mixture around it.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Mix water, sugar, vinegar, salt, garlic and thyme. Place pork in 5–6 qt slow cooker; pour mixture around it.
numbered_cooking_steps: Cover and slow cook on LOW 8–10 hr or until pork is fork-tender and easily shreds (often around 195–205°F, a tenderness target, not minimum safety temperature).
Shred with clean forks and blend with 1–1.5 cups of defatted cooking juices.
Taste and adjust salt if necessary.
recipes.initial_safe_doneness: Whole pork minimum 145°F plus 3 min rest; cook much longer to shred easily
recipes.before_freezing: Divide hot pork into shallow containers; refrigerate promptly until cold, then portion with its cooking juices.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Freezer-safe bags with pork and juices, flattened to <1 inch where possible, air expelled; freeze flat.
recipes.thawing: Fridge 12–24 hr; if thawing in cold water, cook/reheat immediately.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered saucepan 8–12 min on medium-low from thawed to 165°F; stir in juices.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Exposed fibers dry and oxidize.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Juices coat shredded fibers; flattened packs freeze faster.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Serve on rolls; add any sauce at table after checking ingredients.

recipes.name: Sweet Tomato BBQ Shredded Chicken
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Whisk tomato paste, water, sugar, vinegar, salt, garlic and molasses until uniform. Cover raw chicken with sauce.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Whisk tomato paste, water, sugar, vinegar, salt, garlic and molasses until uniform. Cover raw chicken with sauce.
numbered_cooking_steps: Place chicken and sauce in a lidded baking dish. Preheat oven to 350°F.
Bake covered 35–45 min, until thickest chicken reaches 165°F.
Shred in the pan; stir into sauce and bake uncovered 5 minutes to reduce excess water.
recipes.before_freezing: Chill promptly; freeze shredded chicken fully coated in thick sauce.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Freezer-weight bags in 2–3 cup portions; press out air and freeze flat.
recipes.thawing: Fridge overnight.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered saucepan 8–12 min on medium-low to 165°F; add 1 tbsp water only if needed.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Thin sauce may form ice crystals and bread can become soggy.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Reduce sauce before packing; freeze filling and bread separately.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Serve on toasted buns or in baked potatoes.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Mild BBQ Chicken Thighs
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Pat thighs dry; toss with oil, salt and garlic. Whisk tomato paste, honey, vinegar and water for a glaze.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Pat thighs dry; toss with oil, salt and garlic. Whisk tomato paste, honey, vinegar and water for a glaze.
numbered_cooking_steps: Preheat oven to 400°F; line rimmed baking sheet.
Arrange chicken in one layer and brush lightly with half glaze. Bake 15 minutes.
Brush with remaining clean glaze; bake another 8–15 minutes until center reaches 165°F.
recipes.before_freezing: Cool rapidly; portion with a spoonful of cooking juices or extra cooked glaze.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Snug freezer boxes or vacuum freezer bags for cooled chicken, with thin sauce layer.
recipes.thawing: Fridge overnight.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Covered 325°F oven 15–20 min to 165°F; spoon juices over chicken.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Overcooking on reheating leads to dry chicken.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Thighs retain moisture better than very lean breasts.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Add steamed peas, fresh rice or potatoes.

recipes.name: Honey-Garlic Chicken Freezer Kit
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic, vinegar and oil. Coat raw chicken thoroughly inside a clean freezer-weight bag; do not precook.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic, vinegar and oil. Coat raw chicken thoroughly inside a clean freezer-weight bag; do not precook.
numbered_cooking_steps: When ready to cook, completely thaw sealed kit in refrigerator. Preheat oven to 400°F.
Pour chicken and marinade into 9x13-inch dish in a single layer; use all of the raw marinade only because it will be fully cooked.
Bake 25–35 min to 165°F at the thickest portion. For thicker glaze, transfer cooking juices to saucepan and bring to a full boil, then simmer to thicken.
recipes.initial_safe_doneness: 165°F chicken; fully boil any sauce from raw marinade
recipes.before_freezing: Seal and freeze immediately after assembling raw chicken and sauce. Do not bring raw kit to room temperature.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Freezer-weight gallon zip bag; press out air, double-bag if needed; freeze flat.
recipes.thawing: Refrigerator 18–24 hr in a tray; cook soon after thawing.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: This is raw: bake after thawing per instructions, do not treat as a ready-to-eat reheat meal.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Very sweet sauce can burn; raw chicken may release water.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Covered marinade reduces oxygen exposure; bake in one layer, then reduce juices for better texture.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Add cooked fresh rice and broccoli.

recipes.name: Mild Teriyaki Chicken Freezer Kit
ingredients: 2 tbsp cold water (add on cooking day)
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Whisk soy sauce, sugar, honey, vinegar, ginger, garlic. Add thighs; freeze raw marinade/chicken. Reserve cornstarch and cold water off-freezer for finishing.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Whisk soy sauce, sugar, honey, vinegar, ginger, garlic. Add thighs; freeze raw marinade/chicken. Reserve cornstarch and cold water off-freezer for finishing.
numbered_cooking_steps: Thaw raw kit in refrigerator; preheat oven to 400°F.
Put chicken and marinade in baking dish in one layer; roast 25–35 min until chicken reaches 165°F.
Transfer pan juices to saucepan and bring to rolling boil. Mix cornstarch with cold water and whisk in; simmer 1–2 min to thicken. Serve chicken with glaze.
recipes.initial_safe_doneness: 165°F chicken; boil used raw marinade juices
recipes.before_freezing: Freeze uncooked sauced meat right after assembly.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Freezer-weight bag flat with air pressed out; avoid overfilling.
recipes.thawing: Thaw in refrigerator 18–24 hr.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Cook raw kit in 400°F oven as described; never simply warm it.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Sugar scorches and watery thaw drippings dilute sauce.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Thicken heated sauce after cooking rather than freezing a cornstarch gel.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Fresh rice and steamed broccoli.

recipes.name: Golden Oven Chicken Tenders
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Mix yogurt with half salt and garlic. Toss chicken in yogurt mixture. Mix panko, remaining salt and oil in separate shallow bowl; coat tenders.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Mix yogurt with half salt and garlic. Toss chicken in yogurt mixture. Mix panko, remaining salt and oil in separate shallow bowl; coat tenders.
numbered_cooking_steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a rimmed sheet pan.
Lay breaded tenders on rack or parchment, spaced apart; bake 12 minutes.
Flip; bake 6–10 additional minutes until center reaches 165°F and crumbs are lightly browned.
recipes.before_freezing: Chill on rack so steam escapes, then tray-freeze in a single layer until firm.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Transfer frozen tenders to labeled freezer zip bag, push out air, add parchment between layers.
recipes.thawing: Reheat directly from frozen; thawing makes coating wetter.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: 400°F oven 12–18 min from frozen on rack; reach 165°F; avoid microwave if crispness matters.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Breading absorbs thaw moisture and loses crunch.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Tray-freezing and dry oven reheating limit sogginess.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Dip in onion-free and pepper-free condiment.

recipes.name: Homemade Baked Chicken Nuggets
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken breast cut into 1-inch nuggets
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Mix salt and garlic with yogurt and coat nuggets lightly; mix crumbs and butter. Press chicken into crumbs.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Mix salt and garlic with yogurt and coat nuggets lightly; mix crumbs and butter. Press chicken into crumbs.
numbered_cooking_steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line sheet pan; arrange coated nuggets without crowding.
Bake 10 min, flip, and bake 6–10 min more until 165°F internal and golden.
recipes.before_freezing: Cool on wire rack; tray-freeze separately before bagging.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Freezer zip bag with minimal air; double wrap if storing near 3 months.
recipes.thawing: Keep frozen until reheating.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: 400°F oven on rack 10–16 min from frozen to 165°F.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Moisture in crumbs causes loss of crunch.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Rack cooling and dry heat restore surface dryness.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Serve ketchup only after checking its ingredient label.

recipes.name: Chicken Pot Pie Filling, Crust on Serving Day
ingredients: 2 cups low-sodium chicken stock verified without onion or pepper additives
1 cup diced carrots, cooked until tender
1 refrigerated pie crust for serving day (do not freeze touching filling)
recipes.oven_bake_time: 25–35 min after filling has been reheated; 10 min rest
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Melt butter in saucepan; whisk flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in stock and milk; simmer gently until thick (4–6 min). Fold in cooked chicken, peas, tender carrots, thyme and salt; simmer 2 min. Crust stays separate.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Melt butter in saucepan; whisk flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in stock and milk; simmer gently until thick (4–6 min). Fold in cooked chicken, peas, tender carrots, thyme and salt; simmer 2 min. Crust stays separate.
numbered_cooking_steps: To freeze: cook filling on stovetop as described; do not bake it with the crust.
On serving day, thaw filling in refrigerator. Heat it in a saucepan until 165°F; transfer to 9-inch pie dish and lay the thawed pie crust over it.
Cut 4 steam vents; bake at 400°F 25–35 min, until pastry golden and filling bubbling. Verify center reaches 165°F; rest 10 min.
recipes.before_freezing: Rapidly chill the thick chicken filling without the pastry.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Flat freezer bags or airtight quart-size tubs, leaving expansion headspace.
recipes.thawing: Thaw filling overnight in fridge; thaw purchased crust according to package.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Reheat thawed filling in saucepan to 165°F, place in dish, top with crust, bake 400°F 25–35 min; do not place frozen glass dish into hot oven.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Dairy-thickened sauce might weep; pastry becomes soggy when touching frozen filling.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Thick roux-based filling and separately baked pastry hold textures better.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Top with crust only on cooking day.

recipe_example_source.adaptation_note: Adapted into an original no-onion, no-pepper formulation; source recipe may contain excluded ingredients and is not identical.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup Base, Noodles Added Later
ingredients: 7 cups unsalted onion-free chicken stock or water
6 oz dry egg noodles (add only when serving)
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Add stock, thighs, carrots, optional celery, garlic, thyme, bay and salt to large pot; keep uncooked noodles out of freezer base.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Add stock, thighs, carrots, optional celery, garlic, thyme, bay and salt to large pot; keep uncooked noodles out of freezer base.
numbered_cooking_steps: Bring soup base to gentle boil then reduce to simmer; partially cover 25–35 minutes, until chicken reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken, shred, return to pot; discard bay leaf.
Cool base without noodles and freeze. On serving day, bring thawed base to a full boil; add egg noodles and cook 6–9 min per package until tender.
recipes.before_freezing: Divide into shallow containers and chill quickly before freezing.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Quart freezer-safe tubs or liquid freezer bags; allow expansion space and eliminate extra air.
recipes.thawing: Fridge overnight or heat directly from frozen on stovetop.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Bring liquid to rolling boil; cook fresh noodles in soup; leftovers with poultry must be 165°F throughout.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Cooked noodles soak up liquid and become mushy after freezing.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Keep noodles dry and separately packaged until serving.
recipes.serving_day_additions: Dry egg noodles on cooking day.

recipes.name: Cheesy Chicken and Broccoli Rice Casserole
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white rice (cooked and cooled promptly)
1.5 cups broccoli florets, lightly steamed and well drained
recipes.oven_bake_time: 30–35 min freshly assembled; 35–50 min refrigerator-thawed cold casserole
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Cook rice promptly and chill quickly; cook chicken to 165°F first. Steam broccoli just 2–3 min, drain thoroughly. In saucepan melt butter, whisk in flour 1 min, slowly whisk milk and cook until thick. Stir in 1 cup cheddar, salt and garlic. Combine sauce, rice, chicken and broccoli.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Cook rice promptly and chill quickly; cook chicken to 165°F first. Steam broccoli just 2–3 min, drain thoroughly. In saucepan melt butter, whisk in flour 1 min, slowly whisk milk and cook until thick. Stir in 1 cup cheddar, salt and garlic. Combine sauce, rice, chicken and broccoli.
numbered_cooking_steps: Heat oven to 350°F if serving now. Spray 8x8-inch or 2-quart freezer-to-oven metal pan; spread rice mixture and sprinkle 1/4 cup cheddar.
Bake covered 20 min, then uncovered 10–15 min, until center reaches 165°F.
For make-ahead freezing: freeze assembled but unbaked after all cooked components are quickly chilled; later thaw in refrigerator and bake 35–50 min at 350°F to center 165°F.
recipes.before_freezing: Rapidly chill cooked rice, chicken and sauce components in shallow containers before assembly; never leave rice standing warm. Freeze casserole cold and tightly covered.
recipes.freezer_packaging: Small foil baking pan double wrapped (plastic film then foil; remove plastic before baking); label.
recipes.thawing: Thaw 18–24 hr in fridge; bake in metal pan, not frozen glass.
recipes.reheating_or_day_of_cooking: Remove all plastic. Bake covered at 350°F 25–35 min then uncover 10–15 min or until 165°F center.
recipes.water_ice_texture_risks: Rice can become soft and broccoli watery; cheese sauce may split.
recipes.quality_preservation_reason: Drain broccoli, cook rice just tender, use thick roux sauce and small pans.
recipes.serving_day_additions: No additions needed; add fresh veg separately if desired.

recipe_example_source.adaptation_note: Adapted into an original no-onion, no-pepper formulation; source recipe may contain excluded ingredients and is not identical.

recipes.name: Mild Beef and Bean Tomato Stew
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Heat oil; brown beef and finely grated carrots together. Drain excess fat; stir in tomatoes, beans, water, cumin, garlic, salt and sugar.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Heat oil; brown beef and finely grated carrots together. Drain excess fat; stir in tomatoes, beans, water, cumin, garlic, salt and sugar.
numbered_cooking_steps: Cook ground beef to 160°F as you break it into crumbs over 8–10 min.
Bring combined stew to a gentle boil, reduce to low simmer and cook uncovered 25–30 min, stirring occasionally to thicken.
Cool in shallow portions promptly and freeze.
recipes.before_freezing: Chill in shallow 1–2 cup portions, avoid packing while steaming.

recipes.name: Beef Stew Gravy Base, Add Potatoes Fresh
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck cut in 1-inch cubes
2 cups water plus 1 cup onion-free beef stock
2 cups carrots cut in thick coins
1 lb potatoes added only on serving day
recipes.mixture_before_baking_or_cooking: Pat beef dry and dredge lightly in 2 tbsp of flour; cut carrots. Mix water and verified onion-free stock, tomato paste and remaining flour.
recipes.prep_and_assembly_steps: Pat beef dry and dredge lightly in 2 tbsp of flour; cut carrots. Mix water and verified onion-free stock, tomato paste and remaining flour.
numbered_cooking_steps: Heat oil in Dutch oven; brown beef in batches for 6–10 min total.
Pour in broth mixture; add carrots, thyme, salt and bay leaf. Bring to low simmer, cover and cook 1.5–2 hr until beef fork tender.
